purpose: Convert the top-three residual branches into exact named archival/records-management requests whose answers can change D1-D4 or close the documented fate of a missing data class. No broad UFO browsing and no origin inference are authorized by this contract.

stable_official_archive_anchors: NARA Project Blue Book Case Files series 595466
NARA Sanitized Project Blue Book Case Files series 597821
targets.request_object: Exact NARA file-unit/item NAID(s), title(s), box/roll/page or digital-object URL(s) for the 17 July 1957 RB-47 event, including any cross-reference to OSI or other Air Force investigative files.
targets.success_condition: Official NARA response or Catalog object binds the date/event to an exact file-unit/item and, if available, identifies original sensor media or records explicitly stating their absence/disposition.
targets.forbidden_promotion: Do not promote case 4810 or NARA-PBB1-167 to canonical identifiers until NARA itself binds them.

targets.platform: USS Princeton (CG-59) / Nimitz Carrier Strike Group
named_data_classes: AN/SPY-1 / AEGIS target-track or radar-return records
known_schedule_facts: SSIC 3560 Combat Information Center Logs: destroy when 3 years old in the historical schedule text.
SSIC 3610-3613 cover Electronic Warfare/ESM/ECM/ECCM record families with a mixture of permanent primary-program records and shorter-lived correspondence/routine records.
DAA-NU-2015-0003 later superseded most N1-NU-89-005 items; it was approved in 2018.
The exact 2004 classification of Princeton AN/SPY-1 raw returns is NOT established by these schedule texts.
targets.request_object: Identify the disposition authority/SSIC actually governing USS Princeton CG-59 AN/SPY-1/AEGIS target-track data, CIC logs, EW/ESM records, and related exercise/event recordings on 14 November 2004; identify any transfer, destruction, or disposition documentation for those records.
targets.success_condition: A Navy/NARA records-management authority maps the named 2004 data class to a specific schedule/item and, ideally, a specific disposition/transfer record.
targets.forbidden_inference: Short retention in neighboring record classes does not prove that the missing Princeton radar data were destroyed.

targets.official_primary_anchor: DIA/DoD/JCS message forwarded by USDAO Tehran describing the 19 September 1976 F-4 interception
archive_anchors: NARA RG59 Central Foreign Policy File 1973-1979, electronic telegram and P-Reel index system
NARA RG330 Near East and South Asia - Iran Country Files, 1972-1979, accession TR-0330-2020-0097 / W330-81-0223
targets.request_object: Locate item-level records for 19-20 September 1976 using Tehran, Mehrabad, IIAF, F-4, Shahrokhi, USDAO, ARMISH/MAAG, radar, maintenance, communications and fault terminology; identify any aircraft maintenance/fault, ground-radar, advisory, attaché, or embassy records beyond the already public DIA/JCS narrative message.
targets.success_condition: An official item-level record supplies raw/near-raw radar, avionics/maintenance, communications, or ground-radar evidence with timestamps/configuration sufficient to improve D1-D4, or definitively identifies custody/disposition.
targets.forbidden_substitute: Additional narrative retellings or later witness testimony do not satisfy the gate.

global_success_condition: At least one official response or item-level primary record either makes target geometry materially more replayable or closes the provenance/disposition of a named missing data class.
pattern_registry_rule: Every R5 finding must be classified first as PHENOMENON_PATTERN, EVIDENCE_PIPELINE_PATTERN, SELECTION_CONTEXT, or NEGATIVE_FINDING before any hypothesis update.
canonical_seal: R5 ASKS NAMED RECORDS QUESTIONS. AN ANSWER MUST CHANGE MEASUREMENT OR PROVENANCE, NOT JUST ADD ANOTHER STORY.
